title: Food additives: distribution and co-occurrence in 126,000 food products of the French market
authors: Chazelas E, Deschasaux M, Srour B, Kesse-Guyot E, Julia C, Alles B, et al.
population: 126,556 food and beverage products marketed in France with an ingredient list in the Open Food Facts database, retrieved on 10 April 2019
funder: PhD grant from Paris 13 University (E. Chazelas); post-doctoral fellowship from the Fondation pour la Recherche Médicale (ARF201809007046, M. Deschasaux); French Ministry of Health (DGS Arrêté 29 Novembre 2019); French National Cancer Institute (INCa_14059); European Research Council (ERC CoG ADDITIVES_864219). authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
result: 53.8% of products contained at least one additive and 11.3% five or more. Appendix 7, products containing each additive: citric acid E 330 18,302; lecithins E 322 13,102; E 14XX modified starches 10,100; sodium carbonates E 500 8587; ascorbic acid E 300 7919; xanthan gum E 415 7327; sodium nitrite E 250 7144; diphosphates E 450 6529; pectins E 440 6504; mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids E 471 6060. Specific starches: E 1442 209, E 1422 173, E 1414 55, E 1450 30, E 1412 27, E 1420 19, E 1404 18, E 1440 5, E 1410 1. The footnote and the Discussion state that the number of products containing each specific modified starch may be underestimated because packaging often states only 'modified starch'. E 500 had the highest squared loading (0.64) in cluster 3, 'stabilizers and emulsifiers mostly used in biscuits and cakes'; sodium carbonate (E 500), diphosphates (E 450) and lecithins (E 322) co-occurred in 1667 products, mostly biscuits. The authors describe E 500, E 450, E 503 and E 422 as widely used in biscuits and cakes as acidity regulators, stabilizers and emulsifiers. Additive doses were not available.
